preview: An interview experience for the 2022 Summer Internship (Enterprise Engineering Track) at Morgan Stanley, detailing the online coding assessment and two interview rounds.
content: Morgan Stanley Interview Experience Atharva Patil | C.E. T.Y. B.Tech.- 2023 For 2022 Summer Internship (On-campus) Enterprise Engineering Track 1. Interns PPT: This is one of the most important things to attend. It gives you an insight into the company, its diversity, and its working culture. Most importantly, it’ll help you in choosing the most suitable track. I was asked about the company, why I chose it, and its working culture in my interview. Note: It is better to click screenshots of the ppt and refer to them later. :D There are two tracks to work in at Morgan Stanley: a.) App dev track: The App dev team is tasked with designing, developing, and maintaining applications used by the Firm’s business units. b.) Enterprise Engineering track: EE team provides tools, applications, and platforms such as the Firm’s networks, computing hardware, operating systems, and databases for trading applications, mobile applications, and other end-user applications. Make yourself very clear about the track before the coding round itself! 2. Coding Round (3rd Sep): • The test was conducted on the AMCAT platform(8 am - 10 am). There were four different sections, one extra section for the EE track. • Note: The time mentioned for each section here, is not exact, except for the coding section. (i.) Aptitude section: (20 mins) I solved almost all the questions for this section. It mainly consisted of questions related to probability, PnC, profit/loss, seating arrangements, etc. You can easily find such questions here https://www.indiabix.com/online-test/categories/ Also, for different formulae, you can refer to this page https://www.indiastudychannel.com/resources/78963-List-of-Formulas-usef (ii.) Debugging section: (20 mins) This section involved easy debugging questions. I spent a lot of my time on just a single question. Avoid doing that. If you are unable to solve a question, skip it and go to the next one. (iii.) CS fundamental section: (20 mins) This section consisted of questions related to core CS subjects, such as OS, DBMS, OOPs, CN, etc. These were simple and easy to solve. (iv.) Coding section: (60 mins) This section consisted of 3 coding questions. Q1.) In this question, we needed to find the greatest count of valid parenthesis. I solved it using stack. Eg: For (()))((())) , answer is 3. However, I passed 11/12 test cases. :/ Q2.) In this question, there were different prices listed for each category(representing each row) and we needed to find a minimum total price, which will be the sum of prices from each category. We don't require to choose a minimum from each row always. I was able to solve it completely. Q3) I don't remember this question exactly. I was able to pass 5 test cases for this question. Out of all, 13 students were selected for Round 1 (Interview) from the EE track. 3. Interview 1: Technical Round (1 hour- 6th Sep): (i.) I made a good impression on the interviewer with my resume :D. He liked the formatting and styling used by me. (For making resume, I used overleaf.com) (ii.) Then he asked me to introduce myself. Always be prepared for this part. Try to keep it short and to the point. (iii.) He asked me to explain the whole OOP paradigm with real-life examples by sharing my screen and explaining about the same. (Note: Always be ready to share your screen. Keep either a notepad or an editor open.) (iii.) Then, he asked me what CAN is. I thought for a moment but was unable to answer. Although it was simple if I had known about it. (It is just another Area Network: LAN, WAN, MAN, CAN):p (iv.) Further, he asked simple things related to time complexities, different types of loops, etc. (v.) He told me to create a hierarchical tree for an employee working in a company and discuss different tree traversals. Although, I messed up preorder and inorder, but corrected myself sooner. (vi.) He asked me to differentiate between hashmaps and hashtable. Taking this point further, he asked me how hashmaps are getting stored in memory. (I was able to give just 1-2 points). (v.) Next, we discussed the coding round. He asked me about the difficulties in different sections. (vi.) He asked me to explain number of islands problem. I explained it using dfs and bfs approaches. (vii.)The interviewer asked me to rate myself based on my knowledge in DBMS. (This might be tricky, so rate yourself wisely) I rated myself as 8. Then he further asked me about ACID properties. (vii.) Now, he moved the discussion forward and asked me about client-side debugging, to which I told about google developer tools. He then asked about the difference between HTML and XML. I could list out only a few points. :( (viii.) Then he asked me the differences between abstract classes and interfaces. As I already knew this, so I could answer it nicely. (ix.) Further, he asked me to provide him some innovative and technical solutions concerning this COVID-19 situation. As I had a similar project in progress with this idea, I explained that to him. (x.) Then he asked me about sorting algorithms and told me to code Merge-Sort using classes and objects, which I did. (xi.) Lastly, he asked me if I had any questions. I have already prepared some, so I asked him one. (Always keep few questions ready to ask the interviewer, it shows your interest in the firm). Out of 13, 4 candidates were shortlisted for the next round from the EE track. 4. Interview 2: Professional Fitness Round (1 hour- 6th Sep): (i.) I supposed this round to be easier than my previous round, as I expected simple HR questions for this. However, most of the questions asked by the interviewer were situation-based. (ii.) The interviewer was very friendly and asked to consider it a one-to-one conversation rather than an interview. :D (iii.)He asked me to introduce myself and questions related to my projects, ideas, and innovations in them. (Note: Keep your Github profile active. In my case, the interviewer checked my profile and asked me questions related to it.) (iv.) Further, he asked me various opinion-based questions, mostly related to different scenarios and situations. (v.) At last, he asked me if I have any questions. I asked him two questions. Then for the rest of the time, he was sharing his experience. Results were announced the same day and 2 students were selected for the internship from the EE track. Important points to remember: I. For the technical interview: 1. Refer this doc, it will answer most of your questions regarding preparations and resources https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ALRaoed1yBvtD0g1lTOlxOzpu6WkIIPZO36w7P-mkFs/edit 2. Be prepared with DSA questions. My interviewer mainly focussed on fundamental subjects, but many other people from the same track were asked DSA questions. 3. Don't remain silent. Speak out your thoughts you have. Also, avoid bluffing in front of the interviewer. If you don't know the answer to any question, simply say no. 4. For DSA, I prepared from https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/must-do-coding-questions-for-companies-like-amazon-microsoft-adobe/ Try to practice company-specific questions also from gfg. 5. For OS, DBMS, and OOPs in Java and C++, I prepared from gfg. Be prepared with all the concepts from each of them very clearly. 6. For CN, prepare the basics like the OSI model and what happens when you search for something in your browser. https://medium.com/@maneesha.wijesinghe1/what-happens-when-you-type-an-url-in-the-browser-and-press-enter-bb0aa2449c1a 7. For system design, the resources provided in the below link are enough https://systemdesignprep.com/ 8. Be prepared with your projects and their tech stack thoroughly. II. For the HR interview: 1. Try to maintain eye contact with the interviewer. Try showing hand movements. Never interrupt the interviewer in between. First, let them complete speaking, and then tell your statement. 2. Stick to your answer. The interviewer might try to confuse you by giving counter-examples to your solution. 3. Never hesitate to share your thoughts. Try to focus on what is asked and make it clear with the interviewer. 4. Overall, stay calm. Do not panic. Just enjoy the process and cherish the experience. All the best :D
